whyNoRecord: SSCTR-RWS-B-01 (BLOCKING) must close before V1X-RUN-NATIVE is enabled: a stop for a symptom is not read when another report of the same session conflicts with it, which is the app report plus the watch import of an aborted run. firstReviewConditions.closedPart: On every report that does not conflict with another, a stop with reason SYMPTOM, none, null, unlisted or lower-case is read whatever the expression: time version of an easy, long or quality run, a format of another dose (D-5), native. The screen is REQUIRED and every run session ahead is TIME with WARNING_SIGN_SCREEN_REQUIRED (72 shapes, 0 failures). Listed non-symptom reasons (FATIGUE, PACING, CHOICE, TIME) never raise it. A screen answered the same day as the stop does not clear it; one answered later does; pain at that answer routes clinically. The engine's own row for a time session with a stop is byte-identical to the formats-off entry point (36 of 36, same statuses).
firstReviewConditions.openPart: A symptom stop on a report that conflicts with another report of the same session (CONFLICTED row, or a fresh report the engine quarantines as DUPLICATE_CONFLICT_QUARANTINED) is never read: no screen, native sessions next week. See SSCTR-RWS-B-01.

findings.what: A stop for a symptom (or with no reason, or an unlisted one) is not read when another report of the same session conflicts with it. Case: the athlete stops a run for a symptom and logs it in the app (completed false, stop), and the watch import of the same 30-minute run is bound to the session with completed true. The engine marks the row CONFLICTED and quarantines the other report (facts for neither capacity nor learning). The extension reads only non-conflicted rows, so the warning-sign screen is NOT_RAISED and the next week's sessions are native (up to 4). When the import arrives first, the app report is the quarantined one and its stop is on no row. The frozen engine does not read a stop itself, so nothing routes it. Present in bcac30d as well; not introduced by the cycle.
evidence: p1c-conflict-realistic.mjs: deviceCompletedTrue x {appFirst, deviceFirst, sameReview} x {time, native}: 6 of 6 NOT_RAISED_BY_THIS_EXTENSION; the same pair with the import's completed false or absent: 12 of 12 REQUIRED
p1d-conflict-engine.mjs, p1f-policy.mjs: status MODIFY, no question, provenance.excluded DUPLICATE_CONFLICT_QUARANTINED, next review NOT_RAISED
v1-run-format-index.mjs:100 (executed = !conflicted), :107; ADF section 3.1 (an import binds to the session and merges with the app report)
findings.decisions: r3 RWS3-C4 and values.stops.routes.SYMPTOM; WE3-13, WE3-14; RWS3-G.4 (symptoms use the existing warning-sign screen); the first review's A-01 toClose ('on every run report of the record'). The engine's quarantine withholds credit and learning; it does not withhold a protective reading.
findings.toClose: The extension reads a declared stop on every run report it receives or holds for the athlete, including a row marked conflicted and a fresh report the engine quarantines as a conflict, for the screen requirement only (never credit, never an X-2 count or reset, never sizing). Directed test for the three orders (app first, import first, same review) and both expressions. Or a client contract verified by QRE under which such a pair cannot arise, or the app raises the existing screen itself on any stop for a symptom. Then a narrow recheck by a fresh SSCTR instance, which may issue the enabling record.

findings.what: Under an engine ASK for current eligibility (eligibility unassessed or null; r6-adaptation.mjs:549 'unknown is neither clearance nor illness', the plan kept), the extension delivers native formats (11 of 12 sessions ahead) and says runFormat.prescribing true. V1RC reads the same answer as non-prescribing (SSCTR-V1RC-R-02, v1-run-calibration.mjs:576). The dose is the engine's, but a distance target without a time ceiling is the exposure form r3 bounds, and unknown eligibility is not permission to prescribe it (SSCTR-05, RWS2-G.5, RWS3-G.4).
findings.ruling: Ruling of this review (bounded, nonclinical, reversible; no dose change): while the engine's answer is an ASK whose missing inputs include the current eligibility (including the post-race function check), run sessions are the TIME expression, and runFormat.prescribing follows V1RC's prescribing reading (false under ASK, HOLD, CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED, or a standing F08 hold). An ASK for other inputs (unreported training, block choices, break relations) is unaffected.
findings.evidenceStatus: OUT_OF_SCOPE_OF_LITERATURE (an eligibility-governance convention aligned with SSCTR-05 and V1RC R-02; no sporting claim)

findings.owner: Data / iOS adapter, verified by QRE
findings.what: Two client-side paths still carry a typed figure into V1RC as a measurement. (1) The ADF HealthKit table maps every outdoor workout with a distance to measurement GPS and has no rule for a workout the user typed into Health (HealthKit marks such entries, e.g. HKMetadataKeyWasUserEntered). (2) The entry point and the readers test 'device' differently: a report carrying only canonicalActivityId keeps its figure in distanceKm and V1RC reads it as P1 (band 300), while the extension's own reader reads the same row as manual (sourceQuality MANUAL).
findings.toClose: The adapter maps a user-entered HealthKit workout to measurement MANUAL; one device test serves the entry point and the readers.

findings.what: A whole run slower than 900 s/km on a native continuous target is read UNKNOWN (MEASUREMENT_IMPLAUSIBLE, ask) and neither counts nor resets X-2, though it is far above the estimate (28 of the differential cases lost a pause count, all of this kind, for example 14 km measured over 300 minutes). It needs at least 1.8 x the sizing pace, so it is a tail.
findings.toClose: Re-review trigger: real data showing runs classified MEASUREMENT_IMPLAUSIBLE at the slow edge.

findings.what: When a kept structure no longer passes and the planned prescription hash is unchanged, the fallback is a new selection, which can be another native format inside the week. r2 N10 allows a change inside the week only as a withdrawal to TIME. No case arises today (0 of 171) because the inputs are week-anchored.
findings.toClose: Phase B: any band source that a later entry point hands in (BAND_OF) stays fixed within the week, or that fallback is TIME.

findings.what: Out of A-02's scope: V1RC's standing training recalibration reads a typed work pace (actual.work with measurement MANUAL) as comparable (v1-run-calibration.mjs:150, :175-178). This boundary does not add or change that path; the ADF contract sends no actual.work for native sessions.
findings.toClose: Nothing here; the V1RC owner may look at it in its own re-review.
